subject: BlueHarbor capacity intake — proposed sizing call & next steps
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@blueharbor.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@blueharbor.ai>
Date: 2028-06-11T18:03:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + next step: sizing call

Hi Grace / Ben —

Thanks again for the discovery call this morning. Very helpful to get aligned on our primary use case (real-time customer support augmentation) and the latency sensitivity for peak flows. Quick recap and a proposed next step:

- Primary SLA target: 95th percentile response time under 350ms for end-to-end generation (user -> model -> formatted response).
- Typical prompt size: 300 tokens history + 200 token response budget (average request ~500 tokens).
- Expected steady-state QPS: 8 RPS (480 rpm) with peak bursts up to 60 concurrent requests during high volume windows.
- Priority features: low-latency KV cache reuse, prefix caching for repeated templates, and support for streaming.

Based on that profile, we want to schedule a dedicated capacity sizing call (60–90 minutes) to walk through: workload profile, tokenization/avg lengths, target latency SLOs, concurrency shaping, and whether a dedicated GPU pool vs reserved capacity mix is the right fit.

Proposed slots (all EDT):
- Tue Jun 13, 10:00–11:30
- Wed Jun 14, 15:00–16:30

If those don't work, happy to propose alternatives. I've attached our discovery notes and a CSV export of our current traffic sample (blueharbor-workload-template.csv) to help the sizing conversation.

Lena — looping you for procurement visibility (we may need an internal PO for Dedicated).

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Integrations, BlueHarbor AI
[attachment: blueharbor-discovery-notes.pdf (2 pages)]
[attachment: blueharbor-workload-template.csv (CSV, 3MB)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T21:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next step: sizing call

Samir — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the sample traffic. Appreciate the concrete numbers (they help a lot).

We can run a productive sizing session in 60 minutes if we focus on the traffic sample + latency targets; 90 minutes is safer if you want to cover rollout options and fallback policies. We can also use the call to agree on a mutual action plan.

Candidate slots (I adjusted for Pacific customers; times below are EDT / PDT):
- Tue Jun 13, 10:00–11:00 EDT (07:00–08:00 PDT) — shorter, focused on sizing and perf targets
- Wed Jun 14, 15:00–16:30 EDT (12:00–13:30 PDT) — longer, includes rollout discussion

Can you confirm which you prefer? If you select the Wed longer slot, we'll invite Sergio (infra) and Ben (solutions) and prepare a short checklist:
- tokenization samples and avg token lengths
- peak concurrency traces (5–95th percentiles)
- sample input payload sizes and streaming requirements

I attached a one-page intake template that will speed the call if you can fill the highlighted fields ahead of time. I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm a slot.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-sizing-intake-template.csv]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@blueharbor.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T00:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next step: sizing call

Looping in a quick ops note — I'll own the pool sizing discussion on our side. Two items I'd like BlueHarbor to confirm before the call if possible:

1) Tokenization / model family: which model family are you planning to use (open Llama variant vs decoder-only family)? If you don't have a lock yet we can size for a conservative 1.6x multiplier to account for larger model compute.
2) Burst shaping: do you have a preferred strategy for handling the 60-concurrency bursts (queueing vs autoscaling + reserved burst capacity)? If you can share a short snippet of your concurrency spike window (timestamped) we'll run a quick simulation.

I'll bring metrics from a recent comparable customer so we can show expected throughput curves.

—Ben
Product Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@blueharbor.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@blueharbor.ai>
Date: 2028-06-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next step: sizing call

Thanks Grace / Ben — Wed Jun 14, 15:00–16:30 EDT works for our engineering lead and procurement (confirming now). Please go ahead and send the calendar invite.

Answers to Ben's questions:
- Model family: planning to test an open decoder family initially (tokenization similar to GPT-style byte-pair). We'll call out any change before the call.
- Burst shaping: currently queue-first within our sidecar, but we'd like to review autoscale + reserved burst options on the call. I've attached a 20-minute spike trace that shows the 60-concurrency windows (column headers: ts, concurrent_requests).

Also copied procurement for early alignment on PO and contract timelines.

I'll watch for the invite and the intake template — we'll fill the highlighted fields before the meeting.

Samir
Head of Integrations, BlueHarbor AI
[attachment: spike-trace-sample.csv (1.2MB)]
